Saved. Reflection complete.

What was generalizable here: this was a NEW question category — Treasury monetary-metals stock converted to physical ounces via a "fixed statutory conversion rate." The failure (3584.40 vs 2051.51) is a clean ~1.747x factor, which is the diagnostic signature of dividing the dollar stock by the WRONG statutory silver constant rather than any table-reading or median/price error.

What I saved:
- Skill patch (officeqa-treasury-bulletin): new section "Silver/gold monetary-stock -> physical-quantity via STATUTORY conversion rate" — formula physical_oz = dollar_stock / statutory_rate; silver statutory/coinage rate = $1.2929/fine troy oz (371.25 grains/dollar); the trap of confusing it with Silver-Purchase-Act PURCHASE prices ($0.50, $0.6464, $0.9050, $1.29 ceiling); gold $35 post-1934 / $20.67 pre-1934; the clean-factor diagnostic; median = middle-after-sort; and where the silver stock lives (monetary-statistics exhibit).
- Memory: compact pointer with the key constants for fast cross-session recall.

The one thing I could NOT pin down without the document is which exact statutory rate the gold used (I'd need the actual 1938/1948/1958 silver stock figures and the cited real silver price to back it out). But the skill now tells a future agent to test the gold-implied factor against the candidate constants ($1.2929 first), which is the actionable fix.
